note: Quick, Draw! lollipop 4885340923887616: stroke 0 is the round candy, drawn as one closed loop with a small notch at the top; strokes 1 and 2 are the two long sides of the flat stick, leaving the candy at its lower left; stroke 3 is the short line closing the stick's end. In the film the candy and stick slide left to right across a dark surface while the stick swings from pointing down-right to pointing down-left. The rig places the whole doodle by two points, the candy's centre (head) and the point where the stick leaves the candy (neck), so the candy keeps its size and the drawing turns as one piece with the stick's angle. The stick (strokes 1 to 3) stays joined to the candy at the neck and goes halfway (stretch 0.5) toward lengthening to the tip point. In the film more of the stick shows below the candy near the frame edges than in the middle of the shot, so the drawn stick lengthens a little there and still reaches close to the bottom of the frame; full stretch made it half again as long as the doodle's and doubled the size step. Keys come from measured positions: the candy's centre from the gold disc (from its edge plus a 60 px radius where it is cut by the frame), the stick's top point and axis from the bright stick. Each was fitted with a cubic over the 26 frames, because the footage jitters by up to 9 px from frame to frame. Optical-flow tracking (track true) gave slightly lower pops than track false and is kept.
